note.headline: Credit and the dollar lead a defensive tape as mega-cap tech cracks
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 fell -0.38% and the Nasdaq 100 gave back -0.60% as NVDA dropped -5.47% and MSFT fell -2.20%, while the risk barometer sank to -0.82 on broad credit and dollar weakness. Positioning should respect that the pain is concentrated in high-multiple tech and high yield, not in breadth, which stayed positive at a 1.56 advance-decline ratio.
takeaways: Credit led the risk-off move, with LQD and HYG both making session lows well before equities caught down.
Mega-cap tech dispersion is the story under the index, with NVDA down -5.47% dragging the Nasdaq 100 while financials and health care held gains.
The curve flattened again, 2s10s down -3bp to 32bp, on a bear-flattening shift led by the front end.
The dollar index rose to a session high of 102.217 even as EUR/USD firmed, pointing to broad-based USD demand against EM rather than a G10 story.
note.desk_view:
The tape confirms that credit, not equities, is setting the tone. LQD contributed -2.26 to the risk barometer and HYG printed a session low, both moving ahead of the index-level equity weakness. That ordering matters. When investment grade cracks before stocks do, it tends to reflect funding and duration pressure rather than a growth scare, and the move in the Treasury curve backs that reading: yields rose across 2s, 5s and 10s while 30s held flat, a front-end-led flattening that squeezes carry trades more than it signals a hard landing. The level that decides whether this stays contained is HYG. It closed at a session low of 77.18. A further break there without a matching move in VIX, which actually fell -2.31% to 19.46, would say credit is pricing something equities haven't caught up to yet.

What the session contradicts is the idea that this is a broad risk-off day. Breadth held up, 14 advancers against 9 decliners, and three sectors, financials, health care and staples, posted gains. The damage is narrow and concentrated in the names that carried the index higher all year: NVDA, MSFT, ORCL. That is dispersion, not capitulation. The tell will be whether Monday's session sees credit stabilize while tech consolidates, which would argue for a rotation story, or whether HYG keeps making new lows into a VIX print above 20, which would argue the credit signal is real and equities are the ones mispriced.
watching: Whether HYG and LQD stabilize or extend their slide independent of equity price action.
The 2s10s curve, now at 32bp, for a fourth straight session of flattening.
Dollar index follow-through above 102.217 against EM crosses, particularly USD/BRL and USD/TRY at cycle highs.
Mega-cap tech earnings-adjacent flow, with NVDA's -5.47% move the single largest driver of Nasdaq 100 underperformance.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed at 7520.93, down -0.38%, with the Nasdaq 100 underperforming at -0.60% and the Russell 2000 the weakest major index at -0.68%. The Dow held up relatively better at -0.30% and the NYSE Composite was nearly flat at -0.04%, a gap that says small caps and high-duration tech bore the brunt while cyclically diversified large caps were largely spared.

Sector rotation was clean. Financials led at +0.52%, health care added +0.29%, and staples and energy both posted small gains. Technology was the worst sector at -1.15%, with real estate, utilities and materials all softer. Breadth stayed constructive, 14 advancers to 9 decliners for a 1.56 ratio, but dispersion of 1.64 confirms this was a stock-picker's session inside a down index. AVGO rose +3.91% even as NVDA fell -5.47%, both chip names moving in opposite directions on the same day.
note.rates:
The curve flattened again. 2s10s fell -3bp to 32bp and 5s30s fell -3bp to 59bp, with the move driven by the front end: 2-year yields rose roughly 5bp and 5-year yields rose roughly 3bp while 10-year yields rose roughly 2bp and 30-year yields were unchanged. The 3m10y spread also compressed -3bp to 64bp. This is bear flattening, yields rising everywhere except the long end, which usually reflects a reassessment of near-term policy rather than a growth downgrade.

Breakevens fell across the board. The 10-year breakeven dropped -2bp to 2.20 and the 5y5y forward fell -4bp to 2.15, both touching the low end of their recent range. Real yields firmed in response, with the 10-year TIPS yield near 2.66. The MOVE index jumped +7.50% to 92.43, the single largest move in the volatility complex, and it was the second-largest drag on the risk barometer after LQD. Rate volatility is doing more work than equity volatility right now.
note.credit: Credit was the weakest link in risk assets today. LQD fell -0.76% and sits at the top of the list of negative contributions to the risk barometer, HYG fell -0.43% and JNK fell -0.41%, both US high yield proxies making the session's low list. EMB, the EM sovereign dollar debt proxy, fell -0.61% and ranked among the largest negative contributors alongside LQD and HYG. Leveraged loans were the one bright spot, up +0.10%, but that is a small offset against broad spread widening in both investment grade and high yield.
note.fx: The dollar index rose +0.56% to 102.217, a session high, and ranked as the second-largest negative contributor to the risk barometer after LQD, confirming broad dollar demand rather than a single-pair story. EUR/USD actually firmed +0.22% to 1.117 even as the index rose, so the dollar's strength came against the EM bloc: USD/BRL rose +1.40%, USD/TRY rose +0.18% to a session high of 50.212, and USD/CHF rose +0.67%. USD/CNY eased -0.12% to a session low, the one crack in the broad dollar bid.
note.commodities: Gold fell -1.75% to 4042.60 and silver fell -1.96%, both giving back ground even as credit and equities sold off, an inversion of the usual defensive bid. Copper fell -1.00% and was a meaningful negative contributor to the risk barometer, aluminium fell -3.61%. Energy was soft but orderly, WTI down -0.70% and Brent down -0.81%, while natural gas rose +2.18%. Ags were mixed: soybeans rose +3.76% and corn rose +1.99%, while coffee fell -2.50% and cocoa fell -3.04%.
note.volatility: VIX fell -2.31% to 19.46 and VIX9d dropped -6.74%, both easing even as equities sold off, which argues the index-level vol surface isn't yet pricing the credit stress as an equity problem. VVIX eased -1.83% while SKEW ticked up +0.52% to 151.12, a modest bid for tail protection even as at-the-money vol relaxed. The standout was MOVE, up +7.50% to 92.43. Rates vol is rising while equity vol falls, a split that puts the protection bid squarely in the rates market rather than in stocks.
note.digital: Digital assets sold off in line with the broader risk-off tone. Bitcoin fell -2.11% to 73639.30 and ranked among the larger negative contributors to the risk barometer, Ether fell -3.88%, Solana fell -3.99% and XRP fell -3.80%. The move tracked credit and tech weakness closely, consistent with digital assets trading as a high-beta risk proxy rather than offering any diversification on a day when LQD and HYG also fell.
note.international: Asia closed well before the US stress became visible, and it closed strong: the Nikkei 225 rose +2.87%, the KOSPI jumped +4.39%, and TAIEX added +2.52%. Europe was firmer too, EURO STOXX 50 up +0.60% and the SMI at a session high, up +0.61%, though the FTSE 100 lagged at -0.29%. New York inherited a constructive overnight tape and sold it against weak credit and a bid dollar, a gap between the overnight close and the domestic session that is worth watching into Tuesday.
note.correlation:
The session's defining feature is a correlation break, not a correlation confirmation. Gold fell -1.75% and the dollar rose +0.56% on the same day that credit spreads widened and equities fell, the opposite of the usual flight-to-quality pattern where gold and duration catch a bid against risk-off equity and credit. That combination, a falling gold price alongside rising real yields near 2.66%, says this move is being driven by rate and dollar liquidity conditions rather than a classic growth scare, which would normally see gold and long Treasuries outperform.

A break in this pattern to watch is whether gold recouples with weak credit over the next session. If HYG keeps falling and gold fails to find a bid, it argues real yields are the dominant driver and equities, credit and gold are all being repriced against a single front-end rate move. If gold instead turns higher alongside more credit weakness, that would be the more conventional signal, and would argue Monday's move was a one-day anomaly rather than a regime shift.
